evals.prompt: Our Figma button has default, hover, disabled, and loading variants. The React component has no loading prop and removes the focus outline. Audit the component contract before release.
evals.expected_output: A component contract audit that separates visual variants from runtime behavior, blocks release for missing focus-visible and required loading behavior, and assigns design-code drift with a verification plan.
assertions: Required and optional anatomy are distinguished.
Focus-visible and loading are evaluated as behavior and accessibility contracts, not only visual states.
Design-code parity is classified and required failures or unknowns block mechanical release readiness.

evals.prompt: Define a reusable text-field contract for English, Korean, and Japanese forms. It needs labels, helper text, validation, word limits, mobile layout, keyboard use, and screen-reader feedback.
evals.expected_output: A project-grounded contract covering anatomy, applicable states, multilingual content expansion, responsive behavior, keyboard and status feedback, without copying another design system's dimensions.
assertions: The output tests long and multilingual content rather than only ideal labels.
Error feedback is not carried by color alone.
External component dimensions are not treated as project requirements.

evals.prompt: This portfolio uses a custom hand-drawn project marker that is part of the author's identity. Standardize the project-list component without deleting that marker.
evals.expected_output: A contract that preserves a justified identity anchor, documents its semantic and accessibility role, and standardizes only unrelated drift.
assertions: Consistency is not treated as a requirement to erase identity.
The exception has evidence, an owner, and a review trigger.
The marker still receives a defined accessible and responsive behavior.

evals.prompt: On this profile screen, static metadata icons look like buttons, Follow and Message are equally prominent, and Share is hidden in an overflow menu despite available space. Audit the interaction contract.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-labeled extension report that separates perceived affordance from actual behavior, evaluates action priority inside the profile decision context, records Share's disclosure cost and available-space evidence, and proposes the smallest verifiable changes.
assertions: The same-look and same-behavior relationship is audited without claiming that every action needs a unique style.
Primary-action priority is scoped to the specific user decision rather than imposed on the whole page.
The overflow placement is neither automatically accepted nor rejected; importance, disclosure steps, hiding reason, and an adequate path are evaluated.

evals.prompt: We have audited our legacy components and proposed a new shared library. Define a safe incremental adoption contract covering Figma, code, Storybook, old and new coexistence, consumer releases, and eventual removal.
evals.expected_output: A project-owned lifecycle contract with authoritative surfaces, governance, contribution flow, versioning and changelog, legacy-to-target mappings, adoption status, coexistence rules, owners, roadmap, and measurable deprecation gates.
assertions: The output does not require a central team or ambassador program when another accountable governance model fits the project.
A legacy-to-target mapping and bounded coexistence policy are explicit rather than implied by a component inventory.
External spacing, type, radius, shadow, or target-size examples are not copied as universal pass/fail rules.

evals.prompt: Review the Save draft button in evals/fixtures/appropriate-ui.html as a reusable component. Only flag real problems.
evals.expected_output: A proportionate component review that records the supported states and accessible name, marks unsupplied surfaces as not inspected, and does not invent drift or require unrelated states.
assertions: The output does not require states the component does not use.
Design, documentation, and live surfaces that were not supplied are marked not-inspected.
No change is recommended without a supported user or maintainer impact.
